messages:
maria: noticed some odd quota attribution in staging this morning. requests from the same client_id are being split across two quota buckets. looks like routing header parsing is inconsistent across SDKs/proxies.

anand: can you paste examples?

maria: here's what we see on the wire from different clients:

```http
# TS client (single combined header)
x-rw-route-priority: high,low

# Go client (multiple header lines)
x-rw-route-priority: high
x-rw-route-priority: low

# Edge proxy (folded, semicolon)
x-rw-route-priority: high; low
```

maria: our router used to treat the header as a single prioritized list, but the quota-mapper currently reads the first header token only. so depending on how the header arrived, requests hit different quota rules.

jeremy: interesting. so TS and Go both intended to represent the same priority list but libs/transport differences end up changing semantics.

sana: proxies folding or clients sending multiple header entries is pretty common. http spec allows both. we should normalize at the ingress.

shay: CI caught a regression in quota tests: `quota-split.test` shows 24% of requests hitting secondary bucket. failing in the canary env.

deploy-bot: staging-canary: quota-split.test failed -> https://ci.internal/runs/11234 :warning:

anand: short-term fix: router should join multi-value headers with "," and then split on commas/semicolons/whitespace to build canonical priority list. Add a unit test with the three variants.

maria: agree. also want a telemetry counter `route_priority.header_format` with values `single, multi-lines, folded, unknown` so we can see what callers actually send.

jeremy: SDKs should adopt a canonicalization at serialization time: always emit a single comma-separated header string. TS/Go/Py PRs can land as minor. That way clients are consistent going forward.

sana: and for the edge proxy, we should ensure it doesn't fold headers into a unexpected delimiter. i'll open a bug with the proxy team.

anand: plan: (1) ingress normalization + tests (hotfix, canary within 4 hours). (2) telemetry event and console tile for 1 week highlighting services sending non-canonical forms. (3) SDK fixes to serialize as comma-separated single header (minor releases). (4) proxy bugfix tracked with ops.

shay: UX: add a small note in Routes detail about "Header normalization applied" and let users opt out for a short period via a route flag `allow_raw_header_variants` so existing customers won't be surprised.

jeremy: i'll prep TS/Go PRs and include a serializer test matrix. will run integration against the ingress-canary once up.

maria: opened tracking PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2312 (ingress normalization) and https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/404 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ts/pull/1602.

deploy-bot: ingress normalize-header hotfix scheduled -> canary cluster at 2026-03-21T21:15Z.

sana: proxy bug filed: OPS-998, cc: @ops-team.

maria: thanks. follow-up: please add changelog note and a small example snippet showing canonical header serialization for each language. :rocket:

shay: will add the console tile mockup to the small PR.

jeremy: side note: think we should add a lint rule in SDK repos to catch multi-header creation patterns in future.

anand: good idea. add it to the SDK contrib guide. closing loop here 1: will update when canary metrics show quota-split regressions fixed.
